name: common-status-labels-remaining
reviewNotes: v63 selects three Japanese lunar labels: 165 三日月 -> 娥眉月, 168 臥待 -> 十九夜, 169 居待 -> 十八夜. 臥待月 and 居待月 denote the nineteenth and eighteenth lunar nights respectively; do not swap their source indices. Keep 新月, 上弦, 下弦, 十六夜 and the previously translated 滿月 unchanged. All new labels fit three cells. This supersedes the earlier blanket preservation of moon labels; 69 records are now selected. Native field width still requires verification.

v55 source review adds record 171: Japanese 満月 becomes Traditional Chinese 滿月. The other moon-phase labels and their order remain unchanged; 66 records are now selected. This supersedes the earlier note treating all moon labels as identical Han text.

Reviewed all 18 original source sheets through index 179. Select 65 complete status/equipment labels, common messages, animal commands and statistics needing Chinese changes; preserve existing released entries, identical Han-character words including moon phases, units, delimiters and split-name syllables. Record 124 added after v48: native caller at ROM 0x1f115 tests WRAM 0307 bit 04, displays common message 7c via 84a0b9 when blocked, otherwise writes the selected table value to 155a. This is changing a selection, not returning to a place; not yet included in a released ROM.

Indices 36-45 include isolated syllables used to compose names; do not independently translate or reorder these without caller evidence. Add height label 15 with its 08 prefix retained, and render the day-count suffix at 32 as 日 without moving the caller's number. The 62 v46 entries remain unchanged; native layout/composition checks are still required.

This source block is represented by top-level entries in the release manifest. Future integration must follow that owning path, preserve original entry offsets and verify native layouts; the draft compiler only verifies source identities and text controls. Selected status labels are at most four cells plus the original one-cell indentation at record 20.

Retain leading 08 at records 16/20, 06 at records 27/28 and 07 at records 149/150. The presence of a control prefix alone does not classify a record as developer text; these labels and warning messages have visible text. Ignore those controls only for static visible-width measurement.

Record 115 has separate actor and bag-owner names on its first line, sampled at five cells each; its third field is an eight-cell item. Other 09 fields use eight cells and amounts use five digits. These are contextual samples, not verified custom-name bounds. Record 118 retains two leading spaces.
